topline.text: Ofsted's chief inspector has announced a pilot independent complaints review, letting schools challenge whether an inspection's outcome itself was fair - not just how a complaint was handled - after three unions passed no-confidence motions in his leadership this month.

The teacher pay dispute looks resolved: the NEU has paused its strike ballot after the Education Secretary confirmed schools can keep pension-contribution savings to fund the 3.5% 2026/27 award in full, without clawback.
Sheffield's finance and performance committee met Monday on the £602k Firth Park/Parkwood SEND and places expansion flagged yesterday - the decision hadn't surfaced publicly by this morning.
topline.action: Worth a call to the council or Lift Schools for the outcome.

topline.text: Reminder: Sheffield schools break for autumn half term from Monday (26-30 October).

diary.text: South Yorkshire Mayoral Combined Authority Board meets.

items.body: Sir Martyn Oliver has announced that schools inspected in 2026/27 can ask an independent reviewer - contracted by DfE, separate from Ofsted - to look at whether an inspection's outcome was fair, not just how a complaint was handled. Where grading is in question, the reviewer can recommend a report card be set aside and the school reinspected. It follows NEU and other unions' votes of no confidence in Oliver's leadership this month.

The NEU has paused its strike ballot after Education Secretary Lucy Powell confirmed schools can keep savings from reduced pension employer contributions to cover the 3.5% 2026/27 pay award, rather than having them clawed back centrally - which the union is calling a fully-funded rise.

As flagged yesterday, Sheffield's finance and performance committee met on Monday to decide on passing £602,000 of government funding to Lift Schools for three SEND rooms and 30 extra Year 7 places at Firth Park Academy, bundled with a temporary expansion at Parkwood Academy. No decision had been reported publicly as of this morning.
items.action: Worth a call to the council or Lift Schools for the result if either is a feeder or partner.

box.text: Share of state-school teachers in England now working in a school with a two-week October half-term, up from 12% in 2025 and 7% in 2023 - driven mainly by academies setting their own calendars. Sheffield schools are taking the standard one week from Monday.
box.attribution: Teacher Tapp survey of 8,112 teachers, reported this week
